text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 2967779012 — HIGH severity: Multiple GPU OOMs observed during prefill on pool gpu-pool-84 causing container restarts. Triggering on long-context requests. Paging @ryan. Monitor: <https://internal.metrics/redwood/gpu-pool-84>
ryan: I'm oncall, joining bridge now. Any immediate mitigation suggestions?
ana: saw repeated CUDA faults (Xid 79) and containers restarting in a loop for ~20m. Prefill memory spikes to ~95% on large context requests (>64k tokens). Repro locally with a 120k-token prefill that forces huge KV cache.
ryan: Ok. Priorities: reduce incoming pressure and stop restarts. Propose: 1) throttle prefill for pool-84 2) block very large-context routes to that pool 3) scale down runtime batch/prefill limits. Who can apply routing?
jay: I'll add a temporary route rule to divert requests with context_length > 65536 away from gpu-pool-84 and into fallback pools. Applying now: `kubectl patch trafficpolicy gpu-pool-84 -p '{"spec":{"rules":[{"match":"context_length>65536","action":"deny"}]}}'`
deploy-bot: Routing change applied to gpu-pool-84 (rev v42). Rollback window set to 10m.
ryan: Nice. ana, can you change runtime config hot to reduce batch size and max_prefill_tokens?
ana: Applying runtime tweak to hotpool: `curl -s -X POST https://runtime.internal/config -d '{"batch_size":4,"max_prefill_tokens":8000,"prefill_throttle":0.5}'` — applied. Observing metrics.
maya: Customer impact: CS reported two customers experienced 503s in infer-prod-us-east around the spike. Not widespread but visible in high-volume streams. I'm drafting an initial customer note.
liz: Any kernel/driver evidence? Need dmesg / nvidia logs to see if it's user fault or driver.
ana: dmesg shows GPU page fault traces and several `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79` entries around restart times. NVidia logs and nvcrash tarball are being collected.
ryan: Good. Immediate plan: keep throttle and routing for now, drain and rotate suspect nodes one at a time, collect nvcrash + container logs, and prepare fallback to CPU coldmodel if restarts continue. Jay, start node rotation on the hotspot node.
jay: Starting drain for node gpu-node-183: `kubectl drain gpu-node-183 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — node cordoned and pods evicted. ETA ~3m.
deploy-bot: Node drain initiated for gpu-node-183. New node provisioning queued.
ana: Logs uploaded to ticket INC-2026-391: `nvcrash_gpu-node-183.tar.gz` and container logs `prefill-restarter-183.log`. I also grabbed kernel trace snippets.
maya: Sent customer update: "We've identified a memory issue impacting long-context requests; mitigation in progress (throttles applied, node rotation). No data loss. Will follow up with status in 30 minutes." :email:
ryan: If OOM rate reduces with throttles, we'll gradually reopen traffic with lower thresholds. If Xid 79 persists, escalate to drivers/kernel team and consider moving pool to a different instance SKU.
liz: I'll draft a safe-fallback policy that routes >64k contexts to a smaller model or returns a polite error explaining limits. WIP.
ana: After applying runtime change + routing, OOMs dropped from ~12/hr to ~1/hr on pool-84. Container restart frequency decreased significantly. Still seeing isolated Xid 79 traces on gpu-node-183.
ryan: Keep rotation. Jay, cordon and recreate node-183 if it's the hotspot.
jay: cordoned node-183 and triggered reprovision. New node gpu-node-199 booting.
deploy-bot: New node gpu-node-199 provisioned and joined pool-84.
ana: Monitoring: no restarts on the new node for 12m. Error stream dropped to zero in the last 8m.
maya: Customer follow-up sent: "Traffic restored for most customers after throttles + node rotation. We're running extended monitoring and will provide RCA." Customers acknowledged.
ryan: Closing actions: 1) Keep prefill_throttle at 0.5 for 2h 2) keep the routing rule blocking >64k contexts for pool-84 until RCA 3) run extended stress tests in staging for long prompts 4) collect RCA artifacts and schedule postmortem. Handing overnight watch to @ana.
ana: Acknowledged. I'll own RCA doc and overnight monitoring. Starting collection of telemetry and reproduce tests.
ryan: Thanks team. Incident state: mitigating -> under control. Will follow up in postmortem. :thumbsup:
